patch.value: A nested SDK dispatch for another tracker reuses the caller's active extension scope, so the second tracker's guards and extension fields never load

Reported by the Codex review of PR 1764. The active extension scope is one process-local boolean (activeExtensionScope in src/sdk/runtime.ts). runAction, PmClient item-transaction helpers and runInActiveExtensionScope all skip activation when it is set, without comparing the tracker the scope was opened for. A host that opens runWithActiveExtensions for tracker A and then dispatches a mutation for tracker B inside the callback runs it under A's registrations: a beforeMutation guard installed only in B never judges the write, and B's extension fields are unknown. The same call made outside the scope activates B and is refused. The behaviour predates PR 1764; the new finalize step inherits it through the shared rule.

The active extension scope records the resolved tracker root it was opened for; A dispatch or runInActiveExtensionScope call for a different root activates that root's extensions or refuses with a typed error naming both roots, never reusing the other tracker's registrations; A spec installs a refusing guard in tracker B only and proves the nested write is judged; Same-root nesting keeps reusing the scope without a second activation
A write to tracker B is judged by tracker B's guards whether or not a scope for tracker A is open
Inside a scope opened for tracker A, a write to tracker B runs under A's registrations and B's guards are skipped

value.text: Additional scope from the third Codex review of PR 1764: runAction with an explicit cwd holds the activation gate's write slot while its command runs, but does not mark an active scope. A command that then calls runInActiveExtensionScope, runWithActiveExtensions or a plain nested runAction for the same tracker waits for a read slot that cannot open until the command returns. The fix belongs with scope identity: a dispatch should publish the scope (and its tracker root) it already holds, so nested same-root work reuses it.
